# Test-Case Catalog

## Test Case Catalog

This is the authoritative list of test cases the harness must cover. IDs are stable per Decision 7; tests reference them via `#[spec("…")]` annotations once the harness exists in M2. Coverage is enumerated from the code as it ships today (Decision 27 — "code is authoritative"); documented behaviors with no catalog entry are listed as deliberate skips at the end of this section.

Platform coverage column shorthand: **mac+linux** = macOS and Linux (Windows once the harness's Windows path is ready per Decision 4); **mac+linux+windows** = portable from day one.

Tier vocabulary (issue #502, CLAUDE.md rule 5): L1 tests run in the fast tier, `cargo test-fast`. L2 tests are split by whether they reach a **real agent** — **lane 1** is the credential-free `tests/e2e_*.rs` files, `cargo test-e2e`, which CI runs on every PR; **lane-2** entries below are in a file gated `#![cfg(all(feature = "e2e", feature = "e2e-live"))]`, run by `cargo test-e2e-live`, which **runs on a developer's machine and nowhere in CI** — no e2e test reaches a real agent on a runner, and no test credential is registered on this repository (the separately credentialed agent PR reviewer is out of scope; see [`docs/develop/governance.md`](../docs/develop/governance.md#the-automated-reviewer)). Lane 2 is where the real-agent tests live and it is flaky-tolerant. Nothing here is a "pre-PR" tier any more — that obligation was removed with #502 — but this catalog is how you find the tests that cover what you changed, which rule 5 still requires you to run and to name. See [`docs/develop/e2e-lanes.md`](../docs/develop/e2e-lanes.md), and note that a lane-2 test whose preflight cannot be satisfied SKIPS and is counted as a pass.

Demo-reel eligibility marker: a trailing ` [reel]` on an entry's `##### <id> — <headline>` line opts that test into the PRD #180 demo reel (`.claude/skills/demo-reel-adapter`). Eligibility is **opt-in** — the default (no marker) is *not* eligible even for a PTY-attached test that records a cast. Mark a test only if it validates the feature **as a user actually runs and sees it** — a real agent genuinely spinning up (spawn → agent → work) — never a synthetic/stand-in test (`cat`, scripted echo, recorder stubs, terminal-probe, or synthesized hook events). The adapter includes a marked test in the reel only when it *also* has a cast and its source changed on the branch.

### Telemetry export (PRD #1741)

#### telemetry/resources

##### telemetry/resources/001 — Detached work keeps its run identity in resource exports.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_resource_collector.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic Python stand-in with a double-forked CPU-burning grandchild; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** the grandchild is reparented; only it performs a file-triggered CPU burn between samples, and the HTTP/JSON run's CPU growth covers that measured burn within two clock ticks. The run reports named anon/file/shmem PSS with positive anon PSS and shares deck.run.id with the actual agent.run span at the same receiver. With disk metrics disabled, worktree identity stays stable and working-directory paths are absent by default and present as deck.worktree.path after explicit opt-in.
- **Does not assert:** work that exits between samples, exact whole-host CPU totals, cgroup accuracy, protobuf encoding or a hosted backend.
- **Platform coverage:** Linux.

##### telemetry/resources/002 — Unattributed CPU growth covers a cleared detached burn.
- **Layer:** L2 process integration, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_resource_collector.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic double-forked Python burner with a cleared environment; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** the fixture is reparented and has no OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES. A continuously sampled, shared unattributed bucket has no deck.run.id, live processes, positive anon PSS and named anon/file/shmem points; its cumulative CPU growth across a file-triggered fixture burn covers the measured burn within two clock ticks.
- **Does not assert:** exact unattributed totals, fixture-specific memory or exclusive process membership: unrelated host processes can contribute CPU and PSS to the same bucket and metrics intentionally omit pids. Does not cover cleared-environment children that remain in a run's ancestry.
- **Platform coverage:** Linux.

##### telemetry/resources/003 — Runs sharing a worktree share one disk series.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_resource_collector.rs`).
- **Agent:** two synthetic shell/cat runs started by the real deck daemon; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** distinct deck.run.id resources carry the same deck.worktree.id returned by the collector's worktree-id command, and exactly one deck.worktree.disk.usage series grows by at least the allocated blocks of an 8 MiB ballast file added between samples.
- **Does not assert:** background disk-walk cadence, hardlink or nested-repository traversal, exact total disk usage or disk attribution per run.
- **Platform coverage:** Linux.

##### telemetry/resources/004 — Real interactive Haiku resource figures join the deck run. [reel]
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 2 (`tests/e2e_resource_collector_live.rs`), developer machine only.
- **Agent:** real interactive Claude Code on pinned Haiku with imported isolated credentials, onboarding and project trust.
- **Asserts:** a directive visibly advances Thinking → Working/Bash → Idle and copies a uniquely named sentinel fixture while the collector runs. At least two samples arrive, with cumulative CPU growing above a pre-task baseline; named anon/file/shmem PSS points (positive anon, file and shmem may be zero) carry the same deck.run.id as the completed agent.run span.
- **Does not assert:** native Claude telemetry, exact CPU or memory values, hosted-backend ingestion, cgroup accuracy or non-Linux collection.
- **Platform coverage:** Linux.

##### telemetry/resources/005 — Terminal run gauges keep their live resource identity.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_resource_collector.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic warm-up and measured shell/cat runs started by the real deck daemon; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** collectors with and without path opt-in first export the warm-up worktree's disk series, proving discovery has answered before the measured run starts, then export that run's live and terminal samples after pane close. Complete resource attributes remain identical, including deck.worktree.id and the opted-in canonical path; terminal process count and all three named PSS gauges are zero, and cumulative CPU does not decrease.
- **Does not assert:** worktree changes during a live run, successful delivery after export failures, or CPU in the final unsampled interval.
- **Platform coverage:** Linux.

##### telemetry/resources/006 — OTLP partial rejection fails once without leaking backend text.
- **Layer:** L2 process integration, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_resource_collector.rs`).
- **Agent:** none; standalone collector and loopback HTTP receiver.
- **Asserts:** HTTP 200 JSON and protobuf partial-success responses rejecting 100 points cause --once to exit non-zero, report rejected and 100 on stderr, omit the unique backend errorMessage sentinel, and make exactly one request to /v1/metrics with the selected content type.
- **Does not assert:** retry policy for transport failures, malformed responses, or hosted-backend behavior.
- **Platform coverage:** Linux.

#### telemetry/otlp

##### telemetry/otlp/001 — No telemetry configuration leaves export and agent enablement off.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** the stand-in receives no OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES or CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY, and the local receiver gets no requests across an export interval after the pane closes.
- **Does not assert:** observing arbitrary destinations outside the isolated receiver.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/002 — Configured export describes the run and its status intervals.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat with synthesized status hooks.
- **Asserts:** visible Thinking and Working transitions produce a completed agent.run with run/pane identity, agent kind, closed end reason, status child spans sharing its trace, status-change events, and service/version/host/schema resource attributes at the local HTTP/JSON receiver.
- **Does not assert:** a hosted collector, protobuf encoding or agent-native telemetry.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/003 — The spawned agent and exported run share the same run id.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell recording its environment.
- **Asserts:** OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES contains a nonempty deck.run.id equal to the receiver's run for that pane, and the configured endpoint reaches the agent unchanged.
- **Does not assert:** a real agent exporting its own telemetry (005).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/004 — Private content stays out of exports and telemetry-module logs while interventions remain visible.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat with synthesized hook content.
- **Asserts:** with HTTP/JSON, distinct sentinels from output, TUI-typed human input, prompt/tool hook fields, pane title, OTLP secret header, file contents printed by the stand-in, command argument, pane cwd directory and an ordinary environment value appear in no received request body, URI, non-authentication header or captured telemetry-module log line; the git branch is sent, as the successor run's `vcs.ref.head.name` (issue #1981 M6), and appears in no URI, non-authentication header or telemetry-module log line; the telemetry exporter's startup log is present, the authentication header arrives as intended and the completed run contains an intervention event. A successor actually reads the private file in the privately named git cwd before its run is exported.
- **Does not assert:** content policies for an external agent's own exporter or daemon log targets outside dot_agent_deck::telemetry and its submodules.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/005 — Real interactive Claude telemetry joins the deck run. [reel]
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 2 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export_live.rs`), developer machine only.
- **Agent:** real interactive Claude Code on pinned Haiku, isolated credentials and project trust.
- **Asserts:** a native inbox task visibly advances Thinking → Working/Bash → Idle and copies a unique fixture sentinel; Claude's own HTTP/JSON metrics or logs and the deck's completed run arrive at the local receiver with equal deck.run.id attributes. At least one trace request has service.name=dot-agent-deck, and those deck-owned requests exclude the task prompt, fixture file contents, sentinel/proof filenames and working-directory path.

##### telemetry/otlp/006 — Claude telemetry defaults respect the user's explicit opt-out.

- **Does not assert:** Claude's native exporter, other agent kinds or OpenCode's native export.

##### telemetry/otlp/007 — Real interactive OpenCode telemetry joins the deck run. [reel]
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 2 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export_live.rs`), developer machine only.
- **Agent:** real interactive OpenCode on `common::opencode_test_model()` (default Haiku), a cheap mini or the subscription-compatible `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` override selected through `DOT_AGENT_DECK_OPENCODE_TEST_MODEL`, isolated imported credentials.
- **Asserts:** a genuine interactive Bash turn visibly works, copies a unique fixture sentinel, replies and returns to Idle; the deck's completed run and OpenCode's own logs or traces arrive at the local receiver with matching deck.run.id, structurally read from their JSON or protobuf resource attributes and service.name=opencode. At least one trace request has service.name=dot-agent-deck, and those deck-owned requests exclude the task prompt, fixture file contents, sentinel/proof filenames and working-directory path.

##### telemetry/otlp/008 — Redirects never forward OTLP exports or custom credentials.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** the configured receiver gets an export and its custom x-honeycomb-team authentication header; a 307 redirect to a different local port results in no request and no authentication sentinel at the target across an export interval.
- **Does not assert:** other redirect status codes or a hosted collector.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/009 — Transient collector failures retry the completed run without duplication.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** a receiver returning two 503 responses with Retry-After and then 200 eventually accepts the completed agent.run; rejected attempts retain the same run id and only one accepted run is delivered across a further export interval.
- **Does not assert:** exact jitter/backoff timing, permanent failures or every retryable status code.

##### telemetry/otlp/010 — Natural exit retains the final published status.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell waiting on an exit gate, with synthesized hooks.
- **Asserts:** after visible Thinking, a final Working hook is published immediately before natural exit; the completed run says exited and includes the Working child interval and status-change event.
- **Does not assert:** a deliberately paused exporter subscriber, real-agent hooks or an exit-code attribute.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/011 — Respawning an orchestration worker mints a new run identity.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic cat orchestrator and environment-recording shell worker.
- **Asserts:** a real delegate CLI call to a clear=true worker replaces its agent; two completed runs share the pane and carry distinct run ids, the first ends closed or unknown, and the replacement receives its own exported run id through OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES.
- **Does not assert:** a real agent consuming the delegated task or the separate pane-restart verb.

##### telemetry/otlp/012 — Graceful daemon shutdown flushes open runs within a bounded process exit.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat; no real agent.
- **Asserts:** the harness identifies and SIGTERMs its own daemon while a run is open; the daemon exits without SIGKILL in under fifteen seconds and the receiver gets the run with end_reason=daemon_shutdown.
- **Does not assert:** shutdown with a stalled git probe, a stalled collector or a wire StopDaemon request.

##### telemetry/otlp/013 — Protobuf exports exclude private content across the binary's export pipeline.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** synthetic shell and cat with synthesized hook content.
- **Asserts:** the same private channels as 004 stay absent from raw HTTP/protobuf request bodies, URIs, non-authentication headers and telemetry-module logs, and as in 004 the git branch is the exception in bodies: the successor run's accepted body carries it. Accepted protobuf bodies contain the original and successor run ids with agent.run, the original run exports a human intervention, the authentication header arrives and the telemetry startup log is captured.
- **Does not assert:** a full protobuf schema decode or privacy of external agents' own telemetry.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### telemetry/otlp/014 — Shell operation metadata classifies safe command shapes without exporting content.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** shell/cat stand-in with synthetic shell-tool and Read hooks.
- **Asserts:** program/word classification of plain commands, assignments/prefixes/segments, the commands of a chained line up to the first that declines, the command a listed wrapper runs and no wrapped command for an unlisted one, program shape filtering and conditional word filtering, the word deny-list, first-line handling, neither program nor word for comments, command substitutions and variable expansions before the first word, or a shell reserved word or `eval` as the program, on both the Bash and Codex `shell` paths, child identity/duration/count and absence of sentinel, private and raw command text from captured bodies.
- **Does not assert:** native hook availability for each agent or nested shell grammar.

##### telemetry/otlp/015 — Polled PR check rollups export CI intervals, results and counters.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).

##### telemetry/otlp/016 — Codex launch activates traces and metrics while preserving user choices.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (`tests/e2e_telemetry_export.rs`).
- **Agent:** PATH stand-in named codex, a recorder linked from where npm installs Codex's launcher (`node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js`), launched directly, through a shell script calling codex by name, and by absolute path.

In-script CODEX_HOME and trace opt-outs take effect; absolute-path launches and a script putting the real Codex's directory ahead of the shim on PATH bypass activation; export off preserves PATH and argv with no shim directory on PATH.

##### telemetry/otlp/017 — Devin launch uses a private temporary metadata-only overlay.

- **Asserts:** scripted and plain launches receive a 0600 overlay preserving JSONC settings, endpoint/resource identity and user OTel choices, excluding header values and disabling content logging by default; the overlay exists while running and is removed at pane close. In-script config-home, enabled:false, metric opt-outs and explicit --config are respected; absolute paths bypass activation; export off preserves PATH and argv without a shim directory.

### Session pull requests

#### session/pr

##### session/pr/001 — The daemon resolves the exact branch PR and serves its state, review and CI checks.
- **Layer:** L2 headless, lane 1 (deterministic).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic cat agent, strict offline gh stub).
- **Asserts:** ListAgents live.pull_request carries the exact branch's open PR in preference to terminal PRs; draft, merged, closed, review decisions, absent review and highest-number fallback are mapped correctly; the winning PR's `statusCheckRollup` (check runs and a commit status) is served as its CI summary, failing first, with per-bucket counts (issue #1781). The stub requires explicit repository, all states and all required JSON fields, `statusCheckRollup` included.
- **Does not assert:** periodic refresh (`session/pr/003`) or TUI rendering.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### session/pr/002 — Missing PR data leaves the daemon healthy and the agent without a badge.
- **Layer:** L2 headless, lane 1 (deterministic).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic cat agent, offline gh stub).
- **Asserts:** default branch, failed gh query, empty response, detached HEAD, non-GitHub origin and non-git directory keep a live agent served with no PR; two completed default-branch probes precede the no-gh assertion. Switching from a resolved PR branch to the default branch, detached HEAD or a new branch whose query fails clears the old PR; a same-key transient failure preserves it.
- **Does not assert:** missing gh executable, real authentication or network failures.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### session/pr/003 — PR polling updates an already-attached client without reconnecting.
- **Layer:** L2 headless, lane 1 (deterministic).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic cat agent, mutable offline gh stub).
- **Asserts:** with DOT_AGENT_DECK_PR_REFRESH_SECS=1, switching an open PR to merged/approved updates ListAgents and sends the full PR to one continuously held event subscription even during continuous non-trigger tool traffic.
- **Does not assert:** the particular event variant or metadata key used, browser invocation or real GitHub latency.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### session/pr/004 — A dashboard card shows the PR with its CI and review, and o opens its URL.
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 1 (deterministic).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic cat agent, offline gh stub and BROWSER recorder).
- **Asserts:** the real TUI displays `#1234 ⊙ ✓ ◉` for an open PR with passing CI awaiting review, with the review cell in inverse video and the CI cell not (issue #1781); o on the selected card invokes BROWSER with the exact PR URL; the same key on a default-branch card spawns no opener and leaves Help usable.
- **Does not assert:** a real browser opening, real-agent execution or reel eligibility.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### session/pr/005 — An interactive Haiku agent visibly works beside its pull request badge. [reel]
- **Layer:** L2 PTY-attached, lane 2 (real agent).
- **Agent:** Claude Code (interactive Haiku; strict offline gh stub).
- **Asserts:** a genuine agent on a fixture PR branch lists the files and reveals a uniquely named sentinel omitted from its prompt; the attached TUI displays that filename together with `#1234 ⊙ ✓ ◉`.
- **Does not assert:** real GitHub authentication or network access, a browser opening, or live PR polling transitions.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### session/pr/006 — A pull request opened from the fork the branch is pushed to is the branch's badge.
- **Layer:** L2 headless, lane 1 (deterministic).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic cat agent, strict offline gh stub).
- **Asserts:** with `origin` on the upstream repository and `branch.feat/x.pushRemote` naming a second GitHub remote, ListAgents live.pull_request carries the `isCrossRepository` pull request whose `headRepositoryOwner`/`headRepository` is that push remote's repository, in preference to a higher-numbered one from a stranger's fork with the same branch name (issue #1779).
- **Does not assert:** TUI rendering (`session/pr/004`); a branch with no push remote, case-insensitive matching or a deleted fork (the `pull_request` unit tests); the worktree reclaimer's side of the same match (`worktree/reclaim/013`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

### Dashboard panes

#### dashboard/pane

##### dashboard/pane/001 — A pane appears in the next free layout region when an agent is started.
- **Layer:** L2 (PTY end-to-end).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic — `StartAgent` over the daemon protocol with a `sleep infinity` stub).
- **Asserts:** rendered card grid shows one new card; the corresponding pane region is visible on the right column.
- **Does not assert:** card text content beyond the display name, color of the status badge, exact pixel coordinates.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### dashboard/pane/002 — Closing a pane via `Ctrl+w` removes its card from the dashboard.
- **Layer:** L2.
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** Ctrl+W opens the close confirmation; navigating from default Cancel to Close and confirming removes the card, and the focused card index stays within bounds.
- **Does not assert:** which card receives focus next (`dashboard/selection/*` covers selection-after-close).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### dashboard/pane/003 — The dashboard pane (tab 0) is never closable.
- **Layer:** L2.
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** `Ctrl+w` from the dashboard tab with no card selected is a no-op: neither the pane-scoped nor tab-scoped confirmation opens, no panic occurs, the dashboard remains rendered, and the tab count is unchanged.
- **Does not assert:** any status-line text.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### dashboard/pane/004 — Card title row carries card number and a status badge, with the display name on its own body row directly beneath.

- **Asserts:** rendered card buffer matches the committed snapshot for a single Working session in the Normal density.
- **Does not assert:** pane content; this is a card layout snapshot only.

##### dashboard/pane/005 — Dashboard card highlight follows the stable `selected_session_id`, not card 0 (PRD #83 M3).

- **Asserts:** with three session cards and a `Tab::Dashboard` whose `selected_session_id` points at the second card (`sess-beta`), `ui::sync_and_derive_selection` derives index 1 (not 0); the rendered snapshot shows the `▸` selection marker and highlighted border on the second card while the first and third stay unselected.

##### dashboard/pane/006 — Card row shows `Dir:` (working directory basename), `Last:` (elapsed since last activity), `Tools:` (tool count), `Prmt:` (latest user prompts).

A second 14-column render proves a newline in `abc\ndef` costs no terminal cell, so all six visible prompt cells render as `abcdef` without an ellipsis.

##### dashboard/pane/007 — A Pi pane's card omits the agent-type badge by default, same as every other agent type (fork-only rename/hide, never pushed upstream — reverses PRD #201 M2.2 for this fork only).

##### dashboard/pane/009 — A history-only session is visibly distinct from a live writable session (PRD #20 M4).

##### dashboard/pane/010 — A pane keeps exactly one card when a hook reports on it without an `agent_id` (issue #398).
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `AppState::apply_event` + ratatui `TestBackend` buffer text assertion).
- **Agent:** none (a tagged spawn placeholder plus one synthetic untagged `WaitingForInput` `AgentEvent`).
- **Asserts:** after an `agent_id: None` event lands on a pane that already carries a tagged session, exactly one session claims that `pane_id`, that session carries the reported `WaitingForInput` status, and the rendered card grid contains exactly one status badge. Before #398 the untagged event minted a second session, so the deck drew two cards for one pane and `build_pane_status` picked between their statuses by `HashMap` iteration order.
- **Does not assert:** that the tagged session keeps its accumulated history (the `pre_f9_hook_with_no_agent_id_*` unit tests in `src/state.rs` pin that half); the `WaitingForInput` command-entry carve-out that reads the collision-hardened join (`orchestration/lock/007`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/011 — A multi-byte-Unicode `session_id` truncates on a char boundary instead of panicking the whole deck (issue #574).
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend`).
- **Agent:** none (a hook event carrying a non-ASCII `session_id`, replayed through `AppState::apply_event`).
- **Asserts:** `apply_event` keys the session map on a producer-supplied `session_id` of nine `α` characters verbatim (no validation between the hook socket and the render), and rendering that card in a three-card deck draws ALL THREE cards — the poisoned card's id shortened to the longest char-boundary prefix within the 11-byte title budget plus an `…`, its two healthy neighbours untouched. Repeats the render across 2-, 3- and 4-byte characters at every ASCII offset that puts byte 11 mid-character. Before the fix `&session.session_id[..11]` panicked inside the render loop, so every frame died and the whole deck went down with it.
- **Does not assert:** any rejection or sanitisation of the id upstream of the render (the id is stored verbatim by design); the OSC-8 hyperlink status line, which is the same defect on a different string (`mouse/hyperlink/001`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/012 — A hostile `display_name` on the hook socket is scrubbed and clamped before it can reach a card (issue #670).
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `AppState::apply_event` + ratatui `TestBackend` via `render_card_grid_to_buffer`).
- **Agent:** none (four synthetic hook events, two of them carrying a hostile `display_name` in `event.metadata`).
- **Asserts:** a name carrying ESC, NUL, CR/LF, DEL and a `U+202E` right-to-left override is stored scrubbed and trimmed, and a 400-character one is stored clamped to `agent_pty::DISPLAY_NAME_MAX_LEN` bytes on a character boundary with a trailing `…`; rendering all four cards through the deck's own `ui.display_names` → `SessionState.display_name` resolution draws four status badges, leaves both neighbouring titles intact, and puts no control character or bidi override in ANY buffer cell. Before the fix the ingest applied only `.filter(|n| !n.is_empty())`, and `U+202E` was measured reaching cell (30, 9) — where a flush writes it to the real terminal and it reorders the text around it.
- **Asserts (issue #833 extension):** the card's *preferred* title source, `ui.display_names`, is defended at the seams that WRITE it rather than at the render seam, for the two of its writers that carry a producer-supplied string into this crate. (1) Rename: `pane::RenameOutcome::applied` — the gate the dashboard dispatch loop mirrors into that map — refuses a name whose only planted character is a `U+202E` bidi override, which the byte-level `is_valid_display_name` check admitted because the override encodes as three UTF-8 bytes each above `0x20`; running that refusal through the same three-arm mirror the loop applies leaves the card titled as it was, with no control character or bidi override in any cell. (2) Session restore: `ui::mirror_saved_pane_name` — the one way the four `run_tui` restore sites now mirror `SavedPane.name` into `ui.pane_names`, from which the dashboard loop fills `ui.display_names` — refuses the same two hostile names, so neither map gains an entry and the restored card falls back to the session's own scrubbed name; before it, those sites replayed the name through `rename_pane` (which rejects it and stores nothing) and then inserted the raw string anyway. Control on both: `  café-агент-日本語  ` is still Applied and `  example-beta  ` still restores, each trimmed to exactly what the controller put on `Pane.name`.
- **Does not assert:** the third writer of `ui.display_names` — the daemon's `list_agents` echo of `AgentRecord.display_name`, which is scrubbed at the wire boundary and covered by `session/live/007`; the fourth — a new-pane spawn, gated by `agent_pty::resolve_display_name`; an orchestration role pane's title, which is inserted raw from `role.name` in the project's own `.dot-agent-deck.toml` and deliberately left so (that file also supplies each role's `command`, so reading it is already consent to execute what it names); the title's display-column fit budget (`truncate_styled_segments`), which is `dashboard/pane/015`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/013 — A declared agent identity fills only the initial `No agent` card badge (issue #308).
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend` buffer-text assertions).
- **Agent:** synthetic neutral and ClaudeCode `SessionState` fixtures with a declared Codex identity.
- **Asserts:** a neutral session plus `Some(Codex)` renders the `Codex` badge and the `reviewer` role name (checked independently — PRD fork#405 moved the role name to its own body row, so there is no combined `Codex · reviewer` string) and no `No agent`; after that session reports `ClaudeCode`, the observed identity renders the `ClaudeCode` badge with `reviewer` still shown and no stale `Codex` label. A neutral session with no declaration retains the pre-#308 `No agent` baseline.
- **Does not assert:** declaration propagation through config, spawn, or daemon dispatch; those end-to-end paths are covered by `codex/spawn/009`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/014 — The role name renders on its own first body row, in `palette::ROLE_NAME`, unconditionally — never on the title row, and never gated by the agent-type badge toggle (PRD fork#405 M1).
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend` + color-aware `insta` snapshot).
- **Agent:** none (a synthetic ClaudeCode/Opus fixture with a friendly display name, plus a `display_name: None` variant for the `id_display` fallback and a both-empty (`display_name: None` + empty `session_id`) variant for the height guarantee).
- **Asserts:** with the agent-type badge toggle ON, the title row carries the `<type> (<model>)` badge and NOT the display name, while the first body row carries the display name styled `palette::ROLE_NAME` (`Color::LightRed`). With the toggle OFF (the default), the title row carries neither the badge nor the name, while the first body row STILL carries the name in the same colour — the unconditional half, and the one most likely to regress. Also asserts `palette::ROLE_NAME` is distinct from every status role colour and every registry `badge_color`, that a card with `display_name: None` falls back to `id_display` on the same row, and that a card with BOTH empty renders a blank identity row (`Line::from("")`) that still occupies exactly one row — the `Dir:` row lands on row 2 either way.
- **Does not assert:** the model/badge segment's own content or toggle wiring (covered by `dashboard/agent-badge/001`/`004`); the embedded terminal pane, which keeps its single-line role title and is out of scope for this PRD; `card_height()`'s exact per-density values (covered by `card_height_001_content_derived_values` in `src/ui.rs`). This catalog ID was originally assigned `dashboard/pane/011` by the commit's own RED round, renumbered to `012` in an earlier re-curation, and renumbered again to `014` at this Stage B upstream sync because `012` was independently claimed there by issue #670's hostile-`display_name` test. The idle-art overlay test this PRD's delta-review (F2) originally added was dropped in an earlier re-curation: `fork-only`'s upstream rebase had already removed the idle-art feature (`src/ascii_art.rs`, the `[idle_art]` config section, `IdleArtPhase`/`IdleArtEntry`/`AsciiArtResult`) by the time this commit was folded in, so the overlay F2 fix and its test no longer apply to anything in the tree.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/024 — Hostile `tool_name` / `tool_detail` on the hook socket are scrubbed and clamped before they can reach a card's tool line (issue #833).
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `AppState::apply_event` + ratatui `TestBackend` via `render_card_grid_to_buffer`).
- **Agent:** none (four synthetic `ToolStart` hook events, two of them hostile).
- **Asserts:** a `ToolStart` whose `tool_name` carries ESC and NUL and whose `tool_detail` carries a `U+202E` right-to-left override, a DEL and a CR/LF is stored on `active_tool` scrubbed (`Ba[31msh` / `src/gnidaer rm -rf /`), and a 100 KiB detail is stored clamped to `untrusted_text::MAX_TOOL_TEXT_BYTES` on a character boundary with a trailing `…`; rendering all four cards draws four `Working` badges, puts no control character or bidi override in ANY buffer cell, and still shows both the hostile card's readable tool line and both neighbours'. Before the fix `apply_event` stored both strings verbatim on `active_tool` AND in the `recent_events` journal that `ui::recent_tool_lines` draws the card's tool line from, while the SAME two strings arriving over the daemon's `list_agents` echo were already scrubbed and clamped (`session/live/007`) — one field, two routes, one of them unprotected.
- **Does not assert:** `user_prompt` at the same ingest, which is scrubbed on neither route and is outside #833; the `daemon status` JSON document and the desktop DTO, two further readers of `active_tool` that this ingest-time scrub also covers but which are not rendered into a terminal cell here.

##### dashboard/pane/025 — A declared-Codex pane with no observed agent type and no first delegation must show "Starting…", not a leftover live status (issue #730).
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend` buffer-text assertions via `render_card_with_declared_agent_to_buffer`).
- **Agent:** synthetic `SessionState` fixture shaped like `insert_placeholder_session_awaiting_report`'s output (`agent_type: None`, `expects_agent_report: true`, `agent_report_activity_seen: false`) with a declared Codex identity, plus a second case built directly via `insert_placeholder_session_awaiting_report` itself.
- **Asserts:** `is_pending` is computed on the raw, observed basis (`session.agent_type == None`) rather than the shown/declared one, so a pane whose role config declares `agent = "codex"` but has not yet been delegated a task still renders "Starting…" — the same `expects_agent_report: true, agent_report_activity_seen: false` shape `dashboard/placeholder/001` already pins for the no-declaration case — instead of falling through to `status_style(&session.status)` (a synthetic `Thinking` fixture, matching issue #730's live evidence). Also asserts the declared Codex badge still renders in this newly-reachable state (the deliberate asymmetry: `is_empty_placeholder` stays on the shown/declared basis so the badge survives, while `is_pending` moved to the raw basis) and that the second `is_pending` use site (the "Waiting for agent to report in…" body line) also reaches the pending state. A second render, built via `insert_placeholder_session_awaiting_report` with `status: Idle` — the shape production actually seeds, since every same-version path that sets `status = Thinking` also clears `expects_agent_report` in the same event — pins that the production-reachable shape shows "Starting…" too. Previously, `shown_agent_type` resolved through `declared_agent_type` before `is_placeholder` was computed, so a declared pane's `is_placeholder` was `false` unconditionally and `is_pending` could never fire.
- **Does not assert:** how a live `session.status` (e.g. `Thinking`) actually reaches a session with no real applied event upstream in the field — the daemon-side/wrapper mechanism, split out of the original issue #730 report and tracked separately as issue #732 (the `suppress_text_status`/Codex-version-drift thread reviewer and auditor both identified as the likely live mechanism); the declared-badge-vs-observed-agent precedence, covered by `dashboard/pane/013`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/026 — A card's number badge renders for every position, not only the first nine (issue #801).
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend` buffer-text assertions via `render_card_grid_to_buffer` and `render_dashboard_cards_to_buffer`).
- **Asserts:** ten cards rendered through BOTH production seams whose internal `card_number` computation the fix changed — `render_card_grid_to_buffer` (drives the real `render_card_grid`, the live single-column deck path) and `render_dashboard_cards_to_buffer` (one card per row, computes `card_number` internally too) — and in each render the tenth card still shows the literal `10` badge. Before the fix, both call sites in `src/ui.rs` capped the value at `if n <= 9 { Some(n) } else { None }`, so `num_prefix` rendered as an empty string for every card past position 9 with no fallback — the badge simply stopped, rather than degrading to some other visual index. Unlike a seam that takes `card_number` as a caller-supplied parameter (e.g. `render_card_to_buffer`), both seams asserted here compute it themselves from render order, so this pins the actual fixed computation rather than only proving two-digit *rendering* was already fine. The `render_card_grid_to_buffer` assertion strips the buffer's row 0 (the deck title, `deck_title_line`) before checking: with 10 of 10 sessions shown, that title itself reads `"— 10 session(s)"`, which coincidentally contains the literal `" 10 "` substring independent of `card_number` entirely — an earlier version of this test asserted against the whole buffer and was found in review to pass identically whether or not the production fix was present, because the title-row coincidence alone satisfied it. The fixture (`role_session`, digit-free names, `tool_count: 0`, a `last_activity` that always clamps `Last:` to `0s`) has no other source of a coincidental `" 10 "` match in the card body. The fix decouples the always-shown display value from the `1`-`9` digit-key shortcut, which intentionally keeps its own scope.
- **Does not assert:** that pressing a digit key 10+ jumps to that card — no such shortcut exists, before or after this fix, and none is added by it; badge color or styling; layout/alignment at card widths narrow enough to truncate a two-digit prefix (`truncate_styled_segments` already handles arbitrary-width truncation and is exercised elsewhere); scrolled/multi-column grid layouts, where `flat_index` still lines up with render order the same way but is not separately re-proven here (`dashboard/grid/*` owns column/scroll layout itself).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/015 — A card title wider in COLUMNS than the title region is ellipsized instead of bare-clipped (issue #357).
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend` + `insta`).
- **Agent:** none (a `SessionState` fixture rendered through `ui::render_card_to_buffer` with a CJK display name, an ASCII control, and a name of VS16 emoji).
- **Asserts:** a card whose display name is `项目目录管理` — 6 scalars, 12 display columns — rendered 40 columns wide leaves 26 cells for the title, and the title is cut to fit with a trailing `…` inside that budget, the two characters past it dropped, the ` ● Thinking ` badge still whole beside it, and the top border exactly one card wide. Before the fix `ui::truncate_styled_segments` counted `char`s, so the 23-character title measured as fitting the 26-cell budget and was returned whole at 29 columns; ratatui then clipped the overhang at the right edge and the card read `· 项 目 目 录 管  ● Thinking` with no `…` and no border fill. The same card with the ASCII name `abcdef` renders untouched, which is the property that keeps every committed card snapshot from churning. And the same card named with eight `❤️` (U+2764 + VARIATION SELECTOR-16, one column per `char` but a two-cell grapheme cluster as ratatui draws it) is also cut with a `…` and keeps its badge: a per-`char` width budget measured those at 8 columns against 16 drawn, passed the title whole, and the badge was drawn over its tail — the same symptom, on input the char count had handled correctly.
- **Does not assert:** the eight `ui::truncate_styled_segments` unit tests beside the function, which own the emoji, combining-mark, keycap, halfwidth-dakuten, ZWJ, control-character, mid-wide-glyph, zero-budget and per-segment-style cases, measured against ratatui's own `Line::width` and `Buffer::set_line`; the `Dir:` / `Prmt:` lines, converted by PRD #339 to a per-`char` width sum and covered by `dashboard/pane/006`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/016 — A card shows its pull request number with state and review glyphs at roomy and narrow widths.
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui TestBackend + insta).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic SessionState).
- **Asserts:** an open, review-required PR shows `#1234 ⊙ ◉` at 80 and 30 columns; snapshots pin both sides of the review/state/stats/omission width boundaries and all lifecycle/review combinations (`✓`, `±`, `◉`), including Unknown (`?`) and absent review.
- **Does not assert:** daemon resolution or browser invocation (`session/pr/*`); CI glyphs (`dashboard/pane/017`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/pane/017 — A card shows its pull request's CI result beside the review, which alone is filled.

- **Agent:** none (synthetic SessionState).
- **Asserts:** every CI result draws GitHub's mark in its colour between the state and the review (`✓` green, `✗` red, `●` yellow, `?` dark grey); the review cell is `REVERSED` and the CI cell is not, so an approval and passing CI differ; a PR with checks and no review shows the CI mark alone; narrowing drops the review, then CI, then the state, keeping the number, with snapshots of each boundary (issue #1781).

##### dashboard/pane/018 — Dashboard cards follow creation order for daemon-minted pane ids (issue #827).
- **Layer:** L1 (in-crate `#[cfg(test)]` unit test of `filter_sessions` over a hand-built `AppState`; no terminal).
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** twelve sessions for `pane-<nonce>-<seq>` ids, created one second apart (nonce decreasing, so id order is the reverse of creation order) and inserted in reverse, come out of `filter_sessions` in `started_at` (creation) order. - **Does not assert:** the `(↑a ↓b)` overflow indicator (covered by `dashboard/grid/003`); the `UiState::columns` navigation agreement (`dashboard/grid/002`); the density ladder's own thresholds (`dashboard/density/*` and the `choose_grid_layout_density_*` unit tests); the stats-bar row the grid reserves but does not draw.

##### dashboard/grid/002 — The column count left/right card navigation reads always equals the column count drawn (issue #588).

The count is derived from the drawn cells, so it is an independent witness rather than a re-run of the layout code. Guards the desync a render-path-only fix produces: the grid looks right and arrow-key movement steps somewhere the user is not looking.

Selecting the last card scrolls the window down and flips the marker to `(↑5)`. Closes the asymmetry the issue names — the scheduled-tasks header signalled its hidden rows while the card grid rendered its title plain.

- **Asserts:** a placeholder session inserted via the plain `insert_placeholder_session` (real `agent_id`, `agent_type == AgentType::None`) — the shape a bare shell pane, an unrecognized command (`sleep 600`, `cat`), or any other non-agent PTY has — seeds `expects_agent_report == false` and renders `"No agent"` / `"Launch an agent to get started"`, never `"Starting…"`. This is the negative case proving the discriminator no longer false-positives on `agent_id.is_some()` alone.
- **Does not assert:** the awaiting-report positive case, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/001`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/003 — `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` (the actual Orchestration-tab wiring, not the detection function in isolation) seeds `expects_agent_report` correctly for a devbox-launched role and a non-agent role.
- **Layer:** L1 (direct call into the production `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` helper; no render).
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** given a two-role `Vec<OrchestrationRoleConfig>` — one role's `command` a devbox-wrapped agent launch (`devbox run claude-sonnet-devbox`, this fork's own real role-command shape), the other a non-agent command (`cat`) — `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` seeds the devbox role's session with `expects_agent_report == true` and the non-agent role's session with `expects_agent_report == false`. PRD #536 follow-up: this is the production call site that must derive its answer from the devbox-aware, presentation-only classifier (`AgentType::from_command_including_devbox`), never from the shared `AgentType::from_command` that also feeds the respawn wrap decision — pinning it here, against the real wiring, is what should have caught the near-miss `spawn_007_hook_learned_badge_does_not_change_respawn_launch` regression before CI did.
- **Does not assert:** the render-level "Starting…" copy (covered by `dashboard/placeholder/001`/`002`); the respawn wrap decision itself (covered by `tests/agent_detection.rs`'s `spawn_007`/`spawn_008`); `AgentType::from_command_including_devbox`'s own classification rules in isolation (covered by `from_command_including_devbox_recognizes_devbox_run` in `src/event.rs`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/004 — Once a "Starting…" placeholder has had real, untagged status-asserting activity, it shows its real status and never reverts to "Starting…" again, even after later going back to Idle.
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `TestBackend` render, driven through `AppState::apply_event`).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic untagged `AgentEvent`s — `agent_type: AgentType::None`, `agent_id: None` — matching Codex's own shape of doing real work before it has reported an agent type or identified its generation).
- **Asserts:** issue #549 — a session inserted via `insert_placeholder_session_awaiting_report(.., expects_agent_report: true)` that then receives a real, untagged status-asserting event (`Thinking`) must render its real status (`"Thinking"`) and stop showing `"Starting…"`, even though `agent_type` is still `AgentType::None`; and once cleared this must hold permanently — a later untagged `Idle` event must render the normal `"Idle"` label and must still not show `"Starting…"` again. Fix round (reviewer F8/F11): a resolved placeholder's body line must not still read `"Launch an agent to get started"` (the coherence gap the fix round closed via `is_empty_placeholder`), and going back to `Idle` must not fall back to `"No agent"` either.
- **Does not assert:** the fresh-placeholder positive case (covered by `dashboard/placeholder/001`); the non-agent negative case (covered by `dashboard/placeholder/002`); the role-wiring seeding of `expects_agent_report` itself (covered by `dashboard/placeholder/003`); a *tagged* producer's event (real `agent_id`) reaching the same session — only the untagged path Codex's pre-first-turn shape actually exercises is pinned here; a detach/reconnect round-trip (the `agent_report_activity_seen` field is carried in `SessionSnapshot` and restored by `seed_hydrated_session`/`resync_hydrated_sessions`, but no L1/L2 test here exercises the hydration path itself); the daemon-synthetic shell-activity path, which is `dashboard/placeholder/005`'s.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/005 — A daemon-synthetic `ShellBusy`/`ShellIdle` pair alone must never resolve a genuinely-empty (non-agent) placeholder.
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `TestBackend` render, driven through `AppState::apply_event`).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic `AgentEvent`s of type `ShellBusy`/`ShellIdle` — `agent_type: AgentType::None`, `agent_id: None` — the daemon's own shell-activity monitor output, the only events a bare shell/`cat`/`sleep` pane can ever produce).
- **Asserts:** issue #549 fix round 2 (reviewer H1) — a session inserted via the plain `insert_placeholder_session` constructor (not `..._awaiting_report`) that receives `ShellBusy` then `ShellIdle` and nothing else must still render `"No agent"` and `"Launch an agent to get started"` afterwards, and `agent_report_activity_seen` must still be `false`. `ShellIdle` asserts a status (it reverts a shell-promoted `Working` back to `Idle`), so a latch keyed on `real_status_assertion` alone — which excludes `ShellBusy`/`Unknown`/`MonitoredWaitStart`/`MonitoredWaitDone` but not `ShellIdle` — let this pair permanently resolve a genuinely-empty placeholder; the fix keys the latch on `AgentEvent::is_daemon_synthetic()` instead, which does exclude `ShellIdle`.
- **Does not assert:** the untagged-hook-event path (a real, non-synthetic status assertion resolving an awaiting-report placeholder), covered by `dashboard/placeholder/004`; the daemon's live-surface `SessionStart` path, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/006`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/006 — The daemon's own flat live-surface `SessionStart` (`spawn::surface_spawned_pane`) alone must never resolve a genuinely-empty (non-agent) placeholder.
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `TestBackend` render, driven through `AppState::apply_event` — no prior `insert_placeholder_session*` call; this event is the session's first and only event, matching how the real event actually reaches an already-attached TUI).
- **Agent:** none (a single synthetic `AgentEvent` of type `SessionStart` — `agent_type: AgentType::None`, `agent_id: None`, `metadata` carrying `DISPLAY_NAME_METADATA_KEY` — the exact shape `spawn::surface_spawned_pane` forges for a freshly-fired scheduled `cat`/unrecognized-command pane).
- **Asserts:** issue #549 fix round 2 (reviewer H1 follow-up) — `EventType::SessionStart`'s match arm in `AppState::apply_event` always asserts a status (`SessionStatus::Idle`, `asserted_status == true`), and `AgentEvent::is_daemon_synthetic()` did not originally recognize this daemon-forged `SessionStart` (only `ShellBusy`/`ShellIdle`/`MonitoredWaitStart`/`MonitoredWaitDone`/the delivery-notice `Error`), so the H1-fixed latch fired on it immediately at session-creation time, before any real hook or shell activity — the actual reason `live_004_real_hook_supersession_keeps_friendly_title` stayed red even after the `ShellIdle` exclusion (`dashboard/placeholder/005`) landed. Fix: `is_daemon_synthetic()` also recognizes a `SessionStart` carrying the `display_name` metadata key — real agent hooks never emit that key (see `DISPLAY_NAME_METADATA_KEY`'s own doc comment), the same discriminator already used for the delivery-notice `Error`. Pins that the card still renders `"No agent"` / `"Launch an agent to get started"` and `agent_report_activity_seen` stays `false` right after this one event.
- **Does not assert:** the `ShellBusy`/`ShellIdle` path, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/005`; the untagged real-hook-event path, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/004`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/007 — A placeholder-insert reaching a pane after its session has already been resolved by a real event must not clobber that resolved state back to "Starting…" territory (issue #724).
- **Layer:** L1 (direct `AppState` state assertions, no render).
- **Agent:** none (a single synthetic, non-daemon-synthetic `AgentEvent` of type `SessionStart` — `agent_type: AgentType::None`, `agent_id: None`, no `DISPLAY_NAME_METADATA_KEY` — matching the shape of a real wrapper fork-time `SessionStart`, the opposite of `dashboard/placeholder/006`'s daemon-forged one).
- **Asserts:** that inserting an "awaiting report" placeholder for a pane whose session already has real, resolved status-asserting activity does not reset `expects_agent_report`/`agent_report_activity_seen` back to their pre-resolution values. `insert_placeholder_session_inner` does an unconditional `self.sessions.insert(...)`, so a placeholder-insert loop reaching an already-resolved pane (the race loser) permanently reclobbers `expects_agent_report` to `true` and `agent_report_activity_seen` to `false`, since nothing else ever clears the flag again — wedging the card at "Starting…" forever.
- **Does not assert:** the reverse ordering (placeholder-insert-before-event), already covered by `dashboard/placeholder/004`; the daemon-synthetic non-resolution case, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/006`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/008 — A placeholder-insert reaching a pane whose session key is already occupied but not yet resolved must still be able to arm "Starting…" (issue #724 fix-round-2 regression guard).

- **Asserts:** an occupied-but-unresolved session entry can still be armed to `expects_agent_report=true` by a placeholder insert (`insert_placeholder_session_awaiting_report`) — the fix for #724 must not make this permanently unreachable, since a blanket "skip if occupied" guard would wedge the card at "No agent" instead of "Starting…" for every pane the daemon has forged a session for ahead of the real spawn-time insert.
- **Does not assert:** the occupied-and-already-resolved case (that must NOT be armed), covered by `dashboard/placeholder/007`.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/009 — A wrapper fork-time `SessionStart` (`Emitter::emit_fork_session_start`, `src/wrap.rs`) alone must never resolve an "awaiting report" placeholder's state.
- **Layer:** L1 (direct `AppState` state assertions, no render — like `dashboard/placeholder/007`).
- **Agent:** none (a single synthetic `AgentEvent` of type `SessionStart` — `agent_type: AgentType::Codex`, `metadata` carrying `SESSION_START_ORIGIN_METADATA_KEY: WRAPPER_FORK_SESSION_START_ORIGIN` — the exact shape `Emitter::emit_fork_session_start` sends the instant `cmd.spawn()` returns, before the wrapped child has done anything).
- **Asserts:** issue #733 — `EventType::SessionStart`'s match arm in `AppState::apply_event` always asserts a status, and before this fix `AgentEvent::is_daemon_synthetic()` recognized only `ShellBusy`/`ShellIdle`/`MonitoredWaitStart`/`MonitoredWaitDone`, the delivery-notice `Error`, and a daemon-forged `SessionStart` carrying `DISPLAY_NAME_METADATA_KEY` — nothing that recognized a WRAPPER-origin `SessionStart` (fork-time or either of issue #243's interface facts, all read via `SESSION_START_ORIGIN_METADATA_KEY`). So the fork-time event alone permanently latched `agent_report_activity_seen` and cleared `expects_agent_report` at spawn time, before the wrapped agent had done any real work — one of the mechanisms behind issue #730 (Codex reviewer/auditor panes wedging pre-task with zero real hook events). Fix: `is_daemon_synthetic()` also recognizes a `SessionStart` whose `AgentEvent::is_wrapper_session_start()` is `true` — which already covers all three wrapper-origin markers, not just the fork-time one, since all three are the wrapper observing process startup/interface state rather than evidence of real reported agent work. Pins that `expects_agent_report` stays `true` and `agent_report_activity_seen` stays `false` right after this one event. No render assertion here (unlike `dashboard/placeholder/006`): `resolve_agent_type` stamps a KNOWN `agent_type` (e.g. `Codex`) on every event a real `dot-agent-deck wrap` invocation emits, including this one, so `session.agent_type` becomes non-`None` the moment this event lands regardless of this fix — that independently flips `render_session_card`'s raw-agent_type-gated `is_pending`/`is_empty_placeholder` false, so a render check here would pin an unrelated mechanism. What this fix actually protects is the flag itself, consumed directly by the reconnect/hydration OR-in invariant (`session/live/020`/`021`), the resolved-vs-empty-placeholder distinction for a producer that stays untagged (`dashboard/placeholder/004`), and the model-badge anti-collision guard (`dashboard/agent-badge/008`).
- **Does not assert:** the daemon's own live-surface `SessionStart` (`DISPLAY_NAME_METADATA_KEY`), covered by `dashboard/placeholder/006`; the two interface-fact wrapper-origin markers (`WRAPPER_INTERFACE_READY_SESSION_START_ORIGIN` / `WRAPPER_INTERFACE_SETTLED_SESSION_START_ORIGIN`) in isolation — excluded by the same `is_wrapper_session_start()` predicate this fix uses, but not separately pinned by a dedicated test here; a genuine, non-wrapper-origin status assertion still latching correctly, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/004`; any render-level effect, for the reason given above.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/010 — A wrapper fork-time `SessionStart` alone must never set `session.agent_type` (issue #730).

- **Layer:** L1 (direct `AppState` state assertions, no render — same construction as `dashboard/placeholder/009`, immediately adjacent to it in `src/ui.rs`).
- **Agent:** none (a single synthetic `AgentEvent` of type `SessionStart` — `agent_type: AgentType::Codex`, `metadata` carrying `SESSION_START_ORIGIN_METADATA_KEY: WRAPPER_FORK_SESSION_START_ORIGIN` — the exact shape `Emitter::emit_fork_session_start` (`src/wrap.rs`) sends the instant `cmd.spawn()` returns, before the wrapped child has done anything; identical fixture to `dashboard/placeholder/009`).
- **Asserts:** issue #730 — `AppState::apply_event`'s agent-type assignment excludes any event that is both `EventType::SessionStart` and `event.is_wrapper_session_start()` (`src/state.rs`) — a round-2 widening (reviewer M1 / auditor A) of the guard round 1 shipped, which excluded only the fork-time origin and left the interface-ready/settled origins free to re-stamp `agent_type` within a couple of seconds of fork, undoing the fix almost as soon as it took effect. `Emitter::build_event` (`src/wrap.rs`) stamps `agent_type: self.agent_type.clone()` on every event the wrapper emits unconditionally, including the fork-time `SessionStart`, so without the guard a Codex-identity wrapped pane's `session.agent_type` would flip to `Codex` the instant that event arrives — before the wrapped agent has done any real work. That flip would defeat the render-layer "Starting…" gate in `render_session_card` (`is_untyped_agent = session.agent_type == AgentType::None`; `is_pending = is_untyped_agent && session.expects_agent_report`): once `agent_type` is non-`None` the card falls through to raw `session.status` instead of "Starting…", and Codex's own native hooks do not fire until its first turn completes, so the raw status can display a stale/leftover value (e.g. "Thinking") indefinitely — the symptom issue #730 reports (Codex reviewer/auditor panes wedged showing "Thinking" pre-task, 8h+, zero hook events). Pins that `session.agent_type` stays `AgentType::None` right after this one event, for the fork-time origin specifically.
- **Does not assert:** `dashboard/placeholder/009`'s own fields (`expects_agent_report`/`agent_report_activity_seen`), which this event does not affect differently than that test already pins; any render-level effect of the flag (the render gate this protects, `is_untyped_agent`/`is_pending` in `render_session_card`, is unpinned here — a future render-level regression test belongs alongside the fix); the two interface-fact wrapper-origin markers, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/011`/`012`; the session-creation (`or_insert_with`) path, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/013`; a live Codex wedge reproduced end-to-end (deliberately the smallest direct reproduction, at the `apply_event` level, per issue #730's triage).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/012 — A wrapper output-settled `SessionStart` alone must never set `session.agent_type` (issue #730 round 2).

##### dashboard/placeholder/013 — A wrapper-origin `SessionStart` that CREATES a session (no pre-existing placeholder) must also seed `agent_type: AgentType::None`, not the event's declared type (issue #730 round 2, auditor finding B).

- **Asserts:** `dashboard/placeholder/010`'s guard only runs once a session entry already exists (`session.agent_type == AgentType::None` implies the entry exists); `self.sessions.entry(..).or_insert_with(..)` stamps `agent_type` unconditionally when this is the FIRST event on a session key, which pre-round-2 bypassed the guard entirely on any session a wrapper-origin event itself creates — the exact shape the daemon side sees (no TUI-only placeholder concept), and the same side issue #730's original evidence (`daemon status` showing no live snapshot) was captured against. Pins that a session CREATED by a wrapper-origin `SessionStart` starts `agent_type: AgentType::None`.

##### dashboard/placeholder/014 — A hook event that reaches the deck before an orchestration role pane's placeholder is inserted must leave that pane with one card, carrying the role name and the hook-reported status (issue #806).

- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `TestBackend` render plus a per-pane session count, driven through `AppState::apply_event` and then the production `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` helper, in that order).
- **Agent:** none (a single synthetic `AgentEvent` of type `SessionStart` — `agent_type: AgentType::ClaudeCode`, tagged with the role pane's id and the daemon's `agent_id`, no wrapper-origin or `DISPLAY_NAME_METADATA_KEY` metadata, and a `session_id` that is the agent's own conversation id rather than the pane-derived `pane-<id>` key — the shape a real daemon-spawned agent's boot hook has).
- **Asserts:** the daemon registers an orchestration's role panes before the deck creates their cards, so a hook can reach the deck inside that window. `AppState::apply_event` admits it through the startup-race auto-registration and creates a session under the hook's own id; `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` then inserts the placeholder under `pane-<id>`, consulting only that key, so the pane ends up with two sessions and the deck draws two cards under one role name (the three-cards-for-two-panes grid `status/observing/010` hit in CI). Pins, for a two-role orchestration whose first role's hook arrived early: each role pane has exactly one session; the rendered deck draws each role name exactly once; and the early pane's one card reads its role name with `Idle`, never `No agent` or `Starting…`. No assertion names which map key survives, so skipping the placeholder and adopting the existing session both satisfy it.
- **Does not assert:** the same-key ordering, where the early event already carries the pane-derived id and lands on the placeholder's own entry, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/007`/`008`; a wrapper-origin boot `SessionStart` arriving early, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/015`; a later event from the same agent, still under its original session id, landing on the surviving card, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/016`; which of the two keys the surviving session lives under, or which of its non-rendered fields (`agent_id`, `cwd`, `expects_agent_report`, the two timestamps) the insert carries over — `015` compares the whole session against the placeholder-first order's, and the unit tests beside `AppState::insert_placeholder_session_awaiting_report` in `src/state.rs` do so for every shape the insert reconciles (an untagged early event, a spawn-time agent type, an early session naming a different agent) and for the two it declines; the end-to-end race against a real daemon, which `status/observing/010` avoids by waiting for the placeholder before it writes its hook.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/015 — A wrapper boot `SessionStart` that reaches the deck before an orchestration role pane's placeholder is inserted must leave that pane with one card, in the same `Starting…` state the placeholder-first order produces (issue #806).

- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `TestBackend` render plus a per-pane session comparison, driven through `AppState::apply_event` and the production `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` helper in BOTH orders, on two separate `AppState`s).
- **Agent:** none (a single synthetic `AgentEvent` of type `SessionStart` — `agent_type: AgentType::Codex`, `metadata` carrying `SESSION_START_ORIGIN_METADATA_KEY: WRAPPER_FORK_SESSION_START_ORIGIN`, tagged with the role pane's id and the daemon's `agent_id`, under the wrapper's own `session_id` rather than the pane-derived `pane-<id>` key — the shape `Emitter::emit_fork_session_start` (`src/wrap.rs`) sends the instant its child is forked).
- **Asserts:** the wrapper-origin half of `dashboard/placeholder/014`. `wrap`'s fork-time `SessionStart` is boot provenance, so on its own it creates an untyped, unresolved session that would render `No agent`; the placeholder-first order instead leaves the awaiting-report placeholder armed (`dashboard/placeholder/009`/`010`) and the card reads `Starting…`. Pins, for a two-role orchestration whose first role's wrapper event arrived early: each role pane has exactly one session; the rendered deck draws each role name exactly once; the early pane's session is EQUAL to the one the placeholder-first order builds from the same two inputs — same map key (the pane-derived one), `session_id`, `agent_type` (`None`), `agent_id`, `status`, `expects_agent_report` (`true`), `agent_report_activity_seen` (`false`), `cwd`, `display_name`, `model` (the one the event reported), `outstanding_delegation`, `active_tool`, `tool_count`, `first_prompts`, `last_user_prompt`, the journal's length and the `session_id` each journalled event carries, and the SOURCE of both timestamps; the event is stamped an hour in the past, and `started_at` and `last_activity` must both be the deck's own insert time, as a placeholder's are, never that producer-supplied stamp; and the early pane's one card reads its role name with `Starting…`, never `No agent`.
- **Does not assert:** a real agent hook arriving early, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/014`; the two interface-origin wrapper facts (same `is_wrapper_session_start` path, not separately pinned here); an early session that names a DIFFERENT `agent_id` from the placeholder's, an untagged one, a spawn-time agent type, an event stamped ahead of the deck's clock, or a pane with a remembered start — all compared across both orders by the unit tests beside the constructor in `src/state.rs`; a later event under the original session id, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/016`; the timestamps' exact instants, which differ between two runs by construction; the end-to-end race against a real daemon.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/placeholder/016 — After a role pane's placeholder adopts the session an early hook created, a later event still carrying the agent's original session id must land on that one card (issue #806).

- **Layer:** L1 (direct `AppState` state assertions, no render, driven through `AppState::apply_event` and the production `insert_role_placeholder_sessions` helper).
- **Agent:** none (two synthetic `AgentEvent`s under one session id that is the agent's own conversation id — a `SessionStart` applied before the placeholder insert and a `Thinking` applied after it — each either tagged with the daemon's `agent_id` or carrying none, in all four combinations).
- **Asserts:** the adoption `dashboard/placeholder/014` pins MOVES the early session from the producer's key to the pane-derived one, but the producer keeps sending under its original id; what puts those frames on the moved card is `apply_event`'s reuse guard, which matches by pane and `agent_id` (strict equality for a tagged frame, the issue #398 lone-candidate fallback for an untagged one). Pins, for each of the four tagged/untagged combinations: after the insert the pane's one session lives under the pane-derived key and carries the daemon's `agent_id` — including when the early event carried none, the stamp the tagged follow-up depends on; after the later `Thinking` there is still exactly one session in the state, under the pane-derived key, with status `Thinking`, the same `agent_id`, and both events in its journal; and the placeholder-first order reaches the identical state from the same two events.
- **Does not assert:** any render-level effect, covered by `dashboard/placeholder/014`/`015`; a later event from a DIFFERENT agent, which is `apply_event`'s generation-retire path and unchanged; a later `SessionEnd`, which takes the terminal branch and restores a plain placeholder as before.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

#### dashboard/selection

##### dashboard/selection/001 — While the selection is active, `j` / `Down` selects the next card and wraps at the end.
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `handle_normal_key` dispatch).
- **Agent:** none (synthetic card count).
- **Asserts:** starting active on card 0, `j` advances 0→1, `Down` advances 1→2, and `j` wraps 2→0; the selection stays active (`Some(idx)`) throughout.
- **Does not assert:** how the highlight is drawn (covered by `dashboard/selection/010`); the inactive-start jump-to-first (`dashboard/selection/006`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/selection/002 — While the selection is active, `k` / `Up` selects the previous card and wraps at the start.
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `handle_normal_key` dispatch).
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** starting active on card 0, `k` wraps 0→2 and `Up` retreats 2→1; the selection stays active throughout.

##### dashboard/selection/017 — Enter (Action::Focus) paints the highlight on BOTH decks by setting `selected_index` to the restored target (unified deck behavior).
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `dispatch_action(Action::Focus)` against a recording `PaneController`).
- **Agent:** none (a real Orchestration tab with placeholder role-pane sessions; 3 synthetic dashboard cards).
- **Asserts:** with the deck inactive (`selected_index == None`) and a remembered selection (`last_active_selection == Some(1)`), dispatching `Action::Focus` (what Enter maps to) sets `ui.selected_index = Some(1)` — so the highlight paints — for the ORCHESTRATION deck AND the Dashboard. Pins the unified fix for the PR #151 manual-test regression where Enter never painted the highlight on the Orchestration deck (the role pane was already focused on return, so the reconcile focus-transition guard never re-armed it). Pre-fix RED: `Action::Focus` only focuses the pane and leaves `selected_index == None`.
- **Does not assert:** the per-frame reconcile reactivation path (`dashboard/selection/009`/`014`); the focus side effect itself (`dashboard/selection/003`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/selection/018 — On tab return, the previously-selected deck's PANE is re-focused while the highlight stays clear — symmetric across BOTH decks (unified deck behavior).
- **Layer:** L1 (in-process `switch_tab_with_focus` round-trip + recording `PaneController`).
- **Agent:** none (a second Orchestration tab as the round-trip intermediate; an Orchestration tab; 3 synthetic dashboard cards).
- **Asserts:** after a Dashboard → Orchestration → Dashboard round-trip with a remembered selection (card index 1 → session `s1` → pane `p1`), the controller's last-focused pane is `p1` (the remembered card's pane is re-focused) AND `selected_index == None` (highlight clear). The Orchestration deck already satisfies this (it re-focuses its remembered role pane on return). Pins the unified fix making the Dashboard leave/return symmetric with Orchestration. Pre-fix RED for the Dashboard: it re-focuses nothing on return (its `selected_session_id` is cleared on leave), so the last-focused pane is the intermediate tab's pane, not `p1`.
- **Does not assert:** the per-frame reconcile staying `None` under steady focus; the scroll/viewport reveal of the remembered region.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

##### dashboard/selection/019 — Enter paints the selection highlight on the Orchestration deck after a tab round-trip (real binary).
- **Layer:** L2 (real `dot-agent-deck` binary in a PTY; vt100 grid scraping; `e2e` feature).
- **Agent:** none (an orchestration with two `cat` role panes that stay alive as deck cards; no LLM tokens).
- **Asserts:** open the orchestration, detach to Normal mode, arm a role with `j` (a `▸` marker appears), round-trip Orchestration → Dashboard → Orchestration (the `▸` clears), then press Enter — the `▸` selection marker must reappear on the restored role. This is the real-binary repro of the PR #151 manual-test regression the L1 mocks missed (they never run the real reconcile + focus-restore on an orchestration tab): pre-fix the role pane is already focused on return, so Enter is not a focus transition and the highlight never repaints (the final wait times out).
- **Does not assert:** which role index is restored; the cyan controller focus border; the Dashboard's own Enter-paint (already worked via the reconcile transition and is covered at L1 by `dashboard/selection/017`).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

- **Does not assert:** the real `list_agents`/attach round-trip behind `EmbeddedPaneController::hydrate_pane` (L2 territory); which tab the card belongs to.
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux+windows.

The attached deck's host measurements, supplied by the daemon. Desktop browser coverage of several decks is in `desktop/e2e/host-metrics.spec.ts`; the catalog IDs below name the Rust harness tests.

- **Layer:** L1.
- **Agent:** none.

- **Does not assert:** the sampler's operating-system reads or cache expiry (covered by `protocol/host-metrics/*`).

##### dashboard/host-metrics/003 — An older deck explicitly reports unavailable metrics.
- **Layer:** L1.
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** the overlay says `not available from this deck` beneath `Host of this deck`, without fabricated zero readings.
- **Does not assert:** capability withholding on the wire (covered by `protocol/host-metrics/003`).

##### dashboard/host-metrics/004 — The real TUI displays its daemon's host measurements and closes on Escape.
- **Layer:** L2.
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** the real binary with its lazily spawned daemon renders numeric disk rows for Working root, Worktree parent and Temp root, with a numeric load-per-core row after `m`; Escape removes the overlay and restores the empty dashboard.
- **Does not assert:** real-agent work, remote transport, or exact machine-specific utilisation; this synthetic PTY case is not a reel clip.
- **Timing:** the first wait (the empty dashboard painting after the lazy daemon spawn) has a load-scaled ceiling: 30 s on an idle box, up to 120 s. The deck's daemon-start bound is set 5 s under that ceiling, so a daemon that never binds still prints its error before the wait ends. A starved run once spent 13.6 s on the daemon's pre-bind alone and overran the fixed 30 s (issue #1665).
- **Platform coverage:** mac+linux.

##### dashboard/host-metrics/008 — The overlay's words match the copy the desktop panel is tested against.
- **Layer:** L1 (ratatui `TestBackend` reading `tests/fixtures/host-metrics-copy.json`).
- **Agent:** none.
- **Asserts:** for each shared sample, the overlay shows the shared title and subtitle and exactly the shared label/value rows in order, including the `(warning)` and `(critical)` words of the sample the daemon judged and none for a level it does not know; a deck without host metrics shows the shared not-available sentences. The desktop's `HostMetricsPanel.copy.test.tsx` asserts the same file against the deck card's panel, so a word changed in one client alone fails the other (CLAUDE.md rule 22).
